pr.title: Register a session for agent messages when it subscribes to a pull request
pr.head: a7fa0c89684c68eef0a8b8727a27ec012e425b18

summary: Projector lets your agent sessions message each other. A message reaches only a registered session, one that has an agent.json record with a name, a one-line summary, or both. Until now a session registered only when it ran project agent register, which the message-agent skill does only when messaging comes up. So long-running loops, such as a session fixing its pull requests or a Codex session reviewing a repository, were never reachable.

This pull request registers a session the first time it subscribes to a pull request or a repository with project watch add. That covers an explicit target, --from-output (which Projector's Claude Code mod runs after a push), and the Codex hook that reads a push. The automatic registration has no name. Its summary is generated from the session's subscriptions, such as Fixing acme/app#12, and Projector rewrites it each time the subscriptions change, until the session gives a summary of its own.

Setting agent.auto_register = false in a checkout's configuration turns the behavior off. Any refused precondition, such as no delivery, a signed-out gh, or an error part way, skips the registration silently, and watch add prints what it always printed.

The relay, which carries presence and messages between your machines through sealed hidden refs in the session's own repository, gains a small fix. A presence pushed while a newer summary was waiting no longer marks the record published.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Registration: a session's agent.json, which makes it listable and messageable.
  • Presence: the sealed copy of a registration that the relay pushes so your other machines can see the session.
  • Generated summary: a summary Projector built from subscriptions, marked summary_auto: true in agent.json.
  • Delivery: how a session's events reach it (mod, codex, stream, or none). A session with delivery none is never registered.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One Projector review, at a7fa0c8: clean, with two suggestions and no finding threads.
  • The gate, the full Python suite, and project check passed at this head.

groups.title: Registering a subscriber
groups.kicker: How a first subscription writes a registration with a generated summary
intro: register used to build and write agent.json itself. Its write now lives in write_registration, which both the explicit command and the new automatic path call. So an automatic registration records the same host, machine, checkout, relay_id, and login, and queues the same presence for the relay.

When it is called with no fields, write_registration acts only as a first registration: it returns without writing when agent.json exists or the session subscribes to nothing. register_subscriber wraps it with the preconditions (the setting, delivery, and a login) and swallows any failure, because the subscription it follows has already succeeded.

The generated summary names only the repository of the session's own checkout and counts every other one. The relay publishes presence into that repository, which can be public while another repository the session works in is private.

checks.text: Only the model reaches the PEER MESSAGE event line from this path, and only from a review line whose model passes MODEL_ID. The automatic registration never sets a name.

files.note: Splits the record write out of register, adds the automatic registration, the summary generator, and the rewrite on subscription changes.

checks.text: A registration that gives --summary drops summary_auto, so Projector stops rewriting it. A --name-only registration keeps the flag.

Registration happens only when add writes a new line. A session whose first add ran before anything delivered its events stays unregistered until it subscribes to something new; the review lists this as a suggestion.

Least-detail summaries stay within 120 characters for every role mix the subscription grammar allows, because a fix line always names a pull request. Checked by generating summaries for 2 to 100 repositories and pull requests.
Removing the digest comparison here turns the relay race regression test red.

groups.title: Where subscribing calls it
groups.kicker: The three paths that add a subscription line, and the one function every change goes through
intro: Each path that can add a subscription line calls register_subscriber after the line is written: watch add with a target, watch add --from-output, and the Codex PostToolUse hook. Every change to a session's subscriptions, including the daemon's removal of a merged or closed pull request, goes through edit_subscriptions, which now calls refresh_summary under the session's lock.

files.note: Registers after --from-output adds lines and after a target add writes one. The output is unchanged.
Registers a Codex session when a push's output subscribes it, reading the setting from the hook's cwd.
Rewrites a generated summary whenever the subscription file changes. An OSError from the rewrite never fails the edit.

groups.title: Republishing a changed summary
groups.kicker: How a rewritten summary reaches your other machines, and the race it exposed
intro: A rewrite marks a published presence pending, and Job.maintain now republishes any live session whose record is pending. That exposed a race. A push of an older presence, queued before the summary changed, used to mark the newer record published, so the new summary waited for the lease renewal, up to half an hour.

The outbox now stores a digest of each queued presence beside it. A landed push marks the record published only when the record still produces that digest. An item an older release queued has no digest, so it republishes once and then settles.

files.note: Adds presence_meta and digest, republishes pending presence, and passes each landed digest to mark_published. Keeps summary_auto out of the presence.

checks.text: Removing the pending clause turns the test that a rewritten summary reaches a second machine red.

groups.title: Documentation and skills
groups.kicker: The CLI reference and the skills that tell agents a subscribed session is reachable
intro: docs/cli.md documents the setting, the new behavior of watch add, and a new section on how the summary is generated and kept current. The message-agent skill tells a subscribed session that it is registered already and should give itself a name once it knows its work. fix-pr, review-pr, and review-repo each note that subscribing makes the session reachable.

files.note: Documents agent.auto_register and adds the Registered when it subscribes section.
Explains the automatic registration and how to name the session.

checks.text: The new example leaves out --model, which the skill's first example includes. A registration generated from a fix line has no model, so a session that copies this example still has none. The review lists this as a suggestion.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Registration on each subscribe path, the setting, and the relay race
intro: SubscriberTests covers each subscribe path, the opt-out, a session's own summary left alone, a generated summary that follows adds and removes, the model from a review line, no delivery, a signed-out gh, another repository counted, and 39 subscriptions kept within 120 characters. Two LifecycleTests cover republishing to a second machine and the race. The Codex tests now fake gh as signed out, because a hook's subscription would otherwise ask it for a login.
